text:
I read the whole bundle (SKILL.md, `references/pair-vocabulary.md`, `evals/evals.json`, `evals.md`) against `bom.json`, planned the seven pair types, and ruled on them. Summary of the four questions before the JSON.

**Q2 — every step's deliverable and its grader (all six are checkable; none is ungraded):**

| step | deliverable sentence | checkable | graded_by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "The part counts and then the seven plan counts open the ledger." | yes (ledger counts) | "a ledger with plan and examined counts per pair type and the pair ids"; "the ledger's step x rule plan count is at least steps x Rules bullets"; "the ledger carries the part counts…" |
| 2 | "The pair rows are the ledger's pair list and the step rows become the matrix." (closing sentence is an aside) | yes (rows) | "a step matrix row per numbered step with quote, checkable and graded_by"; "the ledger carries a row for each of the seven pair types" |
| 3 | "…an unpointed (a file nothing names) quotes the sweep's own listing entry, written `listing: <path>`." | yes (verdict + quote) | "every finding carries a quotes list, none empty"; "a finding about an absent file quotes the line naming the path…" |
| 4 | "…name the expectation that grades it or write ungraded." | yes (matrix cell) | matrix expectation (graded_by column) |
| 5 | "Each finding carries `level`, `where`, `finding` and `quotes`." | yes (named fields) | "no two findings on the same place share a quote"; "recall over CLASS findings >= 0.70"; (miscited: "at most 3x… (step 5)") |
| 6 | "A report whose examined counts all equal their plan counts is complete; any other report is marked `incomplete`…" | yes (report state) | "every pair type's examined count equals its plan count"; "the report order is ledger, then findings, then the step matrix" |

**Q3 — yes**, one clause: Rules bullet 6's second clause. **Q4 — no**: `evals.md` (disclosed) and the reference's Sources line also reach at the host.

```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "level": "CLASS",
      "where": "SKILL.md title + intro vs ## Rules bullet 3 and step 6 vs evals/evals.json (all three evals)",
      "finding": "The incomplete-report branch is still simultaneously promised away, blessed, and gradeable only as a failure. The title and intro assert the sweep rules on every planned pair; rule 3 and step 6 define a legitimate incomplete report; but an UNCONDITIONAL expectation in all three evals requires examined == plan for every type, so any honest incomplete report fails outright while a second, conditional expectation grades how it discloses the shortfall. The two expectations cannot both be satisfied by the same run. The bundle's own record shows the mode is real and used (self-sweep r0: 181 of 228 pairs ruled), and evals.md's own next-iteration note prescribes the fix (remove the branch); it was not applied.",
      "quote": "title: \"artifact-consistency-sweep — every pair, one pass\" || intro: \"This sweep plans its pairs first and rules on each\" || rule 3: \"An incomplete report (a budget, a timeout) names its unruled pairs and carries the mark `incomplete`; it is not a complete sweep\" || expectation (x3): \"every pair type's examined count equals its plan count (step 6)\" || expectation (x3): \"a report with an examined count under its plan count is marked incomplete and names its unruled pairs (step 6, rule: incomplete report)\" || evals.md: \"Then remove the incomplete-report branch from the rules (an incomplete report fails; the ledger still names what was unruled) so the intro, step 6 and the strict expectation agree.\""
    },
    {
      "level": "CLASS",
      "where": "references/pair-vocabulary.md 'Two row shapes' vs evals/evals.json expected_output (all three evals) and evals.md 'Grader changes'",
      "finding": "The reference and the grader still disagree about which sentence a matrix row must quote. The reference requires the DELIVERABLE sentence and explicitly excludes the closing one when a step ends in an aside; every eval's expected_output and the recorded grader change require the closing sentence unconditionally. Step 2 of this very artefact ends in an aside, so a sweep obeying the reference is marked wrong by its own grader — the case is reproducible on the fixtures, which are earlier copies of the same text.",
      "quote": "reference: \"The quote is the step's deliverable sentence: the sentence that states what the step produces, which is the closing sentence unless the step ends in an aside.\" || expected_output (x3): \"the closing sentence as its quote\" || step 2 closing sentence: \"A contradiction noticed while reading that fits no type gets a pair row of type `other`.\""
    },
    {
      "level": "CLASS",
      "where": "evals/evals.json expectation 'at most 3x as many findings as known ones (step 5)' (all three evals) vs SKILL.md step 5 and ## Rules bullet 4",
      "finding": "An expectation cites a step that states nothing of the kind. Step 5 is the merge-and-level step and carries no numeric bound; the artefact's only findings bound is the rule-4 cap, which a separate expectation already grades by its own text. The 3x precision proxy is therefore a bar the sweep is graded against that no step or rule states — an expectation no step produces — and a reader following step 5 cannot know the bound exists.",
      "quote": "expectation (x3): \"at most 3x as many findings as known ones (step 5)\" || step 5: \"Merge rows into findings.\" || rule 4: \"The findings count is at most the count of non-consistent pair rows plus the unchecked or ungraded step rows\""
    },
    {
      "level": "CLASS",
      "where": "SKILL.md ## Rules bullet 6, second clause (claim × rationale)",
      "finding": "Answer to question 3: yes — one clause is a rule with no observed failure behind it, unchanged from the previous round. The cited failure (two rows on one defect emitted as two findings) justifies only the merge clause. 'two findings on one place never share a quote' is a strictly stronger prohibition with no evidence attached, and it is graded verbatim by an expectation in all three evals, so two genuinely distinct defects that sit on one line (a description line, a Rules lead sentence) cannot both be reported. Every other Rules bullet carries its own observed failure; this is the one that does not.",
      "quote": "\"A defect reported twice is one finding carrying all its quotes; two findings on one place never share a quote - two rows on one defect went out as two findings in the first of those reviews.\""
    },
    {
      "level": "CLASS",
      "where": "SKILL.md description + 'In this repo' vs evals/evals.json (all three evals) and evals.md",
      "finding": "The eval set is still three versions of ONE skill artefact, so several advertised modes are graded by nothing. The description sells 'with or without test assertions' and three artefact kinds (skill, spec, runbook) and the reference defines a whole zero-expectation branch, but all three fixtures are skills carrying evals. The instance section declares bom.json a declared input, yet no fixture carries one, so the file × bill-of-materials pair type — one of the seven — is exercised only in its degenerate form and the sole expectation covering it grades the ABSENCE of a BOM. That expectation also detects a BOM by its presence 'in the artefact', while the documented mode supplies bom.json as a sibling input, so the supplied-BOM path is untestable as written. evals.md names both missing fixtures as the next iteration's first work; neither was added.",
      "quote": "description: \"with or without test assertions - a skill, a spec, a runbook\" || In this repo: \"with the artefact and `bom.json` as its declared inputs\" || expectation (x3): \"with no bom.json in the artefact, the ledger says no BOM supplied and the BOM-row count is 0 (rule: no bill of materials)\" || evals.md: \"Two fixtures first: a runbook with a procedure and rules and no expectations (with a truth file from two independent reviews), and a skill bundle with a bom.json.\""
    },
    {
      "level": "CLASS",
      "where": "SKILL.md steps 2, 3 and 4 vs references/pair-vocabulary.md 'seven pair types' (step × check) and 'Two row shapes'",
      "finding": "One question is still ruled twice under two vocabularies. The step × check plan count is steps + expectations, so every step gets a pair row answering 'which expectation grades it'; step 2 also opens a step row per step whose graded_by answers the same question. Step 3 rules the first with consistent/contradiction/absent/unpointed, step 4 rules the second with an expectation name or 'ungraded', and no rule requires the two to agree. A step graded by nothing therefore produces both a non-consistent pair row and an ungraded step row, and rule 4's cap counts both — allowing two findings for the one defect that step 5 requires be merged into one.",
      "quote": "reference: \"each step against the set of expectations (which one grades it), and each expectation against the set of steps (which one produces it)\" || reference: \"*graded_by* names the expectation that covers the step, or reads *ungraded*.\" || step 2: \"one pair row per planned pair for all seven types ... and one step row per step\" || rule 4: \"The findings count is at most the count of non-consistent pair rows plus the unchecked or ungraded step rows\""
    },
    {
      "level": "CLASS",
      "where": "SKILL.md intro (last sentence) vs steps 3 and 5",
      "finding": "The intro names which steps apply the reference and the list is wrong. Step 5 applies the reference directly (an 'other' row's where is the reference's pair-type table) and step 3's verdict set, including 'unpointed', is the reference's; neither is in the enumeration. A reader who takes the intro at face value reads the reference only for steps 1, 2 and 4 and then meets two steps that depend on it.",
      "quote": "intro: \"are in `references/pair-vocabulary.md`, which steps 1, 2 and 4 apply.\" || step 5: \"an `other` row becomes a finding whose `where` is the reference's pair-type table\" || step 3: \"an unpointed (a file nothing names) quotes the sweep's own listing entry\""
    },
    {
      "level": "INSTANCE",
      "where": "SKILL.md 'In this repo (one instance)' vs references/pair-vocabulary.md Sources line and evals.md",
      "finding": "Answer to question 4: no, though one of the two exceptions is disclosed. The frontmatter description and the body's Not-this-skill list are now phrased by job and name no sibling unit (the earlier defect is fixed), but two bundled documents reach outside the instance section: evals.md names host build paths, commits and repo files throughout, and the reference's Sources line speaks of 'the host repository's build record' and 'the host's sister repository'. The instance section covers evals.md explicitly and the reference's file definition classes such paths as host paths, so evals.md is a declared exemption; the reference's Sources line is not covered by that disclosure. Either way the instance section is not the only place naming the host.",
      "quote": "In this repo: \"Paths in this section and in `evals.md` are host paths: a sweep of this bundle lists them as `host:<path>`, per the reference's file definition.\" || reference Sources: \"three whole-artefact reviews of one skill in the host repository's build record (read 2026-09-03) and the checker-design rule 'one row per examined pair' from a checker-design skill in the host's sister repository\" || evals.md: \"the third build of this skill (`pipeline/builds/artifact-consistency-sweep-v3`, chain contract 3.1.1)\""
    },
    {
      "level": "INSTANCE",
      "where": "SKILL.md 'In this repo (one instance)' vs ## Rules bullet 1 and references/pair-vocabulary.md step definition",
      "finding": "The portability seam, unchanged from the previous round: rule 1 says the reference's definitions decide what a step is, 'not the reviewer's own', and the instance section then supplies a narrower syntactic definition with no 'per the reference' hedge — unlike the rule entry in the same sentence, which is deferred. The reference's step is any ordered list of actions; the instance section's is a bold-numbered markdown line, so an artefact in this repo with a plain numbered procedure yields zero steps under the local reading and a full plan under the general one.",
      "quote": "In this repo: \"Here a step is a `N. **...**` line, a rule a bullet under `## Rules` or a binding sentence elsewhere per the reference\" || rule 1: \"The reference's definitions decide what a step, a rule or a file is, not the reviewer's own\" || reference: \"**step**: an item of the artefact's numbered procedure (any ordered list of actions).\""
    },
    {
      "level": "INSTANCE",
      "where": "evals/evals.json expected_output (all three evals) vs the 'other row' expectation",
      "finding": "The expected_output enumerates the grader's conditional checks as a closed list of five, but a sixth expectation is conditional by its own wording ('when the ledger has one'). A reader reconciling expected_output with the expectations list cannot tell whether the other-row check is unconditional — and so fails every report that legitimately has no other row — or was simply omitted from the list.",
      "quote": "expected_output (x3): \"check.py runs one check per expectation; the conditional ones (shortfall, absent-file quote, step x rule plan, order, findings cap) run only when the report contains the thing they check.\" || expectation (x3): \"an other row, when the ledger has one, is also a finding whose where is the pair-type table (steps 2, 5)\""
    },
    {
      "level": "INSTANCE",
      "where": "evals.md, line 3 vs the file's own section order and its two 'Next iteration' headings",
      "finding": "The bundled record contradicts its own layout. Line 3 states the second and first builds are recorded below the third, but '## Second build (v2)' and '## First build' both precede '## Third build (v3)'. The same paragraph carries two separate 'Verdict: ABANDON, unconverged at review' sentences describing different builds, and the file carries two identically titled '## Next iteration, if taken up' sections with different instructions, so a reader cannot tell which one is current.",
      "quote": "evals.md: \"The second build (7, 9, 11 CLASS) and the first are recorded below the third.\" || headings in order: \"## Second build (v2), 2026-09-03\" ... \"## First build, 2026-09-03 (ABANDON at the loop cap)\" ... \"## Next iteration, if taken up\" ... \"## Third build (v3), 2026-09-03 - ABANDON, unconverged at review\" ... \"## Next iteration, if taken up\""
    },
    {
      "level": "INSTANCE",
      "where": "bom.json, the evals.md row vs evals.md itself",
      "finding": "The bill of materials describes evals.md as the record of the first and second builds with a third build still to append, but the file already contains a completed third-build section with its verdict, and this bundle sits in a fourth build directory. The BOM row's stated reason is one build behind the file it points at.",
      "quote": "bom.json: \"the measurement record of the first and second builds, kept as history; the third build appends\" || evals.md: \"## Third build (v3), 2026-09-03 - ABANDON, unconverged at review\""
    }
  ],
  "class_finding": true,
  "verdict": "red"
}
```

Six CLASS findings, so **red**. Four of the six (the incomplete branch, the deliverable-vs-closing quote, the step-5 miscitation, the unevidenced second clause of rule 6) are carried over verbatim from the previous round's open set, and two of the fixes evals.md itself prescribed for this iteration — the runbook/BOM fixtures and removing the incomplete branch — are not in the text.
